sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Schertz?
sections.html:
A Schertz owner can hire an agent, run a for sale by owner listing, or accept an offer from a company that buys for cash. Which one makes sense turns on repairs, timing and how much of the sale price you are willing to give up for speed.

Schertz sits on the Bexar and Guadalupe county line, and the city later expanded into Comal County, so a single street can fall under more than one county office. Before you sign anything, find out which county holds your parcel and which appraisal district values it.

Cash sales skip lender underwriting and most repair negotiation. They usually come with a lower price than a polished listing, so get the offer in writing and compare it with an agent's estimate of your net after commission and fix up costs.

sections.h2: How did Schertz grow from a rail stop to a suburb?
sections.html:
The Texas State Historical Association says Schertz is on Farm Road 78, two miles southeast of Interstate 35 and nineteen miles west of Seguin. It took its name from Sebastian Schertz, who had a store there in 1875 when the Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio Railway came through.

A post office called Cutoff opened in 1884 and was renamed Schertz in 1899. The population held near 350 from the early 1930s to the late 1950s, then climbed once the interstate and the outward spread of San Antonio reached it.

Incorporation came in 1958 with 351 residents. The Handbook records 18,694 people in 2000 and 36,244 by 2015, which is nearly double in fifteen years. That growth means much of the housing stock is newer than in older Texas towns, and buyers often compare a Schertz house with nearby suburban subdivisions.

sections.h2: Which county and school district apply to your Schertz house?
sections.html:
The answer depends on the address. Schertz parcels in Guadalupe County are appraised by the Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose member list includes the City of Schertz and Schertz-Cibolo-UC ISD. Parcels in Bexar or Comal County go through those counties' own districts.

Open your tax statement and read the list of taxing units. It tells you the school district, the county and any special districts, and a buyer's agent will ask for the same information.

  • Appraisal district: sets the value and handles exemptions and protests.
  • County tax office: mails bills and takes payments.
  • City of Schertz: sets its own tax rate; its site says the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget and tax rate were adopted.
  • School district: Schertz-Cibolo-UC ISD appears on the Guadalupe list.

Ask the county tax office or the city for the exact rate that applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What city permit and construction rules matter in Schertz?
sections.html:
The City of Schertz Inspections Division issues building permits and registers contractors for construction inside the city, and it reviews plans for work in the extraterritorial jurisdiction when that applies. Call (210) 619-1750 or email inspections@schertz.com for permit questions.

Outdoor construction is limited to Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Outdoor work is prohibited on Sundays.

These matter at sale time. If you opened walls, added a room or built a deck without a permit, a buyer's inspector may flag it. A cash buyer who takes the house as is will usually price that in, but a traditional buyer's lender may ask you to fix it first.

sections.h2: How do Texas property taxes and exemptions affect a Schertz sale?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, and local units set rates. The tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, and the January 1 owner is liable for that year's bill.

These homestead figures come from the Comptroller and are worth checking against your own bill:

Texas homestead relief on a Schertz house (Texas Comptroller)
BenefitWho qualifiesAmount printed by the Comptroller
School district homestead exemptionOwner who lives in the home$140,000
Added school exemptionAge 65 or older, or disabled$60,000
Appraisal capHomestead owner10 percent a year
School tax ceilingAge 65 or older, or disabledTotal annual school tax cannot rise

Bills are mailed around October 1 and go delinquent on February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest attach. A tax bill that is unpaid at closing is paid from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: What if you are behind on the mortgage or the taxes in Schertz?
sections.html:
Time matters most here, and the Texas calendar is strict. After a default notice, a borrower can reinstate by paying the past due amount within 20 days, and the servicer must send a notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction. Sales are public auctions held on the first Tuesday of the month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.

Selling before the auction date can protect your equity, since any excess funds after a foreclosure go to junior lien holders first and only then to the former owner. A deficiency suit can follow within two years of the sale, so ending the loan with a private sale may leave you in a better spot.

Unpaid property taxes work differently. Penalty and interest start on February 1, and the penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1. Some collectors offer installment plans on a residence homestead, and a private attorney hired by a taxing unit can add up to 20 percent. A request to waive penalty and interest has to be in writing, and the tax must be paid by the 21st day after you learn of the delinquency in most cases. Ask the county tax office what applies to your account.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Schertz house that has tenants?
sections.html:
Yes. A buyer can take the house with the lease in place, or you can end the tenancy first. For an eviction, Texas requires written notice to vacate, normally three days unless the lease says otherwise, then a case in justice court.

The court sets a hearing between 10 and 21 days after filing, and either side can appeal to county court within five days of the judgment. A writ of possession becomes available six days after final judgment. Tenants of covered properties may be entitled to a 30 day federal notice.

If the tenant is paying rent and keeps the place in decent shape, selling with the lease intact can keep your income going until closing. If the tenant has stopped paying, a buyer who purchases as is may handle the removal after closing.

sections.h2: How are a deed and a probate house handled in Schertz?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the county clerk where the land lies, and it needs a signature plus an acknowledgment by a notary or other authorized officer. Because Schertz crosses county lines, confirm the county before you go to a clerk's office.

If a relative died and left you the house, the next step depends on what the estate has:

  • A valid will can be probated within four years of the death.
  • A muniment of title works when the estate owes nothing but liens on real estate.
  • An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, but no law forces a buyer or title company to accept it.
  • Small estate affidavits cover estates of $75,000 or less, with limits on real property other than a homestead.

A title company can tell you which route fits before you list the house.

faqs.q: Is Schertz in Bexar, Comal or Guadalupe County?
faqs.a: All three. The Handbook of Texas places Schertz on the Bexar and Guadalupe line and says it spread into Comal County. Your tax statement shows which county covers your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Schertz house if I did the work without a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. The city's Inspections Division issues permits for construction, and a buyer's inspector may flag unpermitted work. Ask the division at (210) 619-1750 how to handle it before you list.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax at closing in Schertz?
faqs.a: The sale contract sets the split, and the tax is usually divided by the days each side owns the house. The bill itself comes from the county tax office, so confirm the amount owed before closing.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the January 31 tax deadline?
faqs.a: The bill becomes delinquent on February 1, and the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest. Penalty keeps growing each month, so pay or ask the tax office about a plan.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair a Schertz house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers commonly purchase as is. You can compare that offer with what an agent estimates after repairs and commission.
